metadata.name: dsh-auto-summary

paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: summarize a session at a token threshold and hand it off to a fresh agent,
always keeping the original first prompt.
# dsh-auto-summary

A third-party **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** bundle that watches each finished agent
turn, measures the

session's token usage, and — once a session crosses a token
threshold — writes a handoff brief with

one auxiliary model call and starts a
fresh agent whose initial prompt is that brief.

The summary always carries the session's **original first user prompt**, quoted
verbatim, so a conti
nuation agent never loses the task it is continuing.

- No DSH source changes: ships as an external bundle (`dsh.bundle.patch`).
- No session mutation: th

e summarized conversation gets no new events and is not
compacted.
- Recursion-safe: handoff agents

are subagents, and subagent sessions are skipped.
- Fail-open: a failed summary or spawn is logged a
nd retried on the next turn.
## Features

| **Turn-end trigger** | Runs after a `turn/end` event, i.e. after each finished piece of work. |
|

**Token threshold** | Defaults to **100,000,000** tokens; measured from the durable session log. |
|
**Two metrics** | `total` (cumulative provider-billed tokens, default) or `context` (current reques

t pressure). |
| **First prompt guaranteed** | Read from DSH's `titleInput` projection (survives com

paction) and force-appended to the handoff task even if a custom template omits it. |
| **Fresh agen
t** | Started through `ctx.subagents.startActivation` with the `spawn` provider; the brief is its fi

rst user message. |
| **No conversation pollution** | The summary call is a hand-built `ctx.llm.stre

am()` request with no session id and no purpose tag. |
| **Re-arm, not spam** | After a successful p
ass the session re-arms one threshold higher, so a long session produces one handoff per additional

threshold, not one per turn. |
| **Dry run** | `dryRun: true` logs what would happen without calling
the model or starting an agent. |
## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` (declared through `engines.dsh: ^0.2.1-rc.5`).
- The profile must mount the servi

ces the plugin reads. The shipped
`dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app` composition does:
`agents`, `llm`, `ses

sionProjections`, `subagents`, `tokenMeter`.
- A subagent provider — `spawn` ships with the base pro

file and is the default.
- A routed provider/model for the summary call: the session's latest
`reque

st/header` route is used unless `summary.provider` / `summary.model` are
configured.

### From GitHub (recommended)

nd package managers block dependency build scripts, so the
repository must ship its build output.

After installation the bundle appears in the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`
list and its `auto-summ

ary` row mounts. Restart the app if the Plugins page says

cked up at the next composition (restart, or toggling

Every field has a default, so the bundle mounts with no configuration. To
configure it, restate the

row in the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` (this layer
is applied after the bundle's):

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

1. **Observe.** The plugin subscribes to the post-commit `session/event` feed at
the root context, s

o it sees every session. It reacts only to `turn/end`.
2. **Gate.** Failed/aborted turns are skipped

by default, and sessions whose
durable header marks them as subagent children
(`origin: 'subagent'`

or `delegationDepth > 0`) are skipped — otherwise the
handoff agent's own turn would trigger anothe

r handoff forever.
3. **Measure.** `total` reads `{ totals }` from the `tokenUsage` session
projecti

on (cache-read/write buckets included); `context` reads
`ctx.tokenMeter.measure(session).totalTokens

`. Both are replay-based and make
no model call.
4. **Summarize.** The first prompt is read from the

`titleInput` projection
(which retains the first human message across compaction), falling back to

the
derived history. The transcript keeps only direct human prompts and assistant
text, newest-first

inside the character budget. One hand-built
`ctx.llm.stream()` call produces the brief; the request

carries no
`sessionId`, no `purpose`, and no tools, so neither the parent conversation
nor DSH's ti

tle/compaction consumers are affected.
5. **Hand off.** The task is delivered as the fresh agent's i

nitial prompt via
`ctx.subagents.startActivation`. The host owns identity, capacity, delegation
dept

h, cataloging, and settlement; the plugin never calls `ctx.agents.create`
and never disposes the chi

ld.
6. **Re-arm.** A successful pass sets the next threshold to
`observedUsage + thresholdTokens`; a

failure leaves the threshold armed and is
retried on the next completed turn.
## Limitations

- Summary quality and wording depend on the summarizer model; the original first
prompt and the hand

off structure are guaranteed by the plugin, the prose is
not.
- The trigger ledger is process-local.

After a restart, a session whose
cumulative usage is already above a threshold is re-evaluated on i

ts next
completed turn.
- With `metric: context`, re-arming still uses cumulative usage, so a sessio

n
normally receives at most one context-pressure handoff until its billed total
grows by another thr

eshold.
- A handoff agent still consumes the host's subagent capacity
(`maxActiveSubagents`, default

8); a rejected activation is logged and retried
on the next completed turn.
- The first prompt come

s from the shipped `titleInput` projection. A profile that
disables `dsh-session-title` falls back t

o compacted history, where an already
compacted first prompt may no longer be present.
